title: Quantization technical review - NyxSoft
topics: KV cache interactions with quantized models
summary: Redwood SE and AE ran through quantization tradeoffs for NyxSoft's 13B/70B inference workloads. Focus on GPTQ/AWQ accuracy, INT8/FP8 latency/cost, and implications for KV caching and batching in their VPC/on-prem environment. Next steps: run benchmark on NyxSoft sample prompts, share secure quantization benchmark sheet, schedule pilot test, and send SOC2 / network diagram.
action_items: Priya Shah: run GPTQ pipeline (4-bit + groupwise) against NyxSoft 13B finetuned model and share raw evals - due 2027-12-06
Marcus Li: provide sample prompt corpus and representative throughput/latency SLOs and test dataset link - due 2027-12-01
Tom Ellis: send pricing for Dedicated reserved capacity and estimated cost delta for INT8 vs FP8 configurations - due 2027-12-03
Alicia Park: flag top 100 prompts for accuracy-sensitive routes and annotate acceptance thresholds - due 2027-12-04
next_steps: Redwood to run internal AWQ experiments and compare to our GPTQ baseline and share a one-page executive summary
Schedule 1-hour pilot kickoff the week of 2027-12-08 to run live throughput tests in NyxSoft VPC
Share SOC2 + network architecture doc and on-prem packaging checklist
NyxSoft to confirm list of allowed egress/IPs for pilot
transcript:
Meeting header: 2027-11-29 16:00 PST — Duration 48 min — Attendees: Tom (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Liam (Redwood Solutions Eng), Alicia (NyxSoft ML Lead), Marcus (NyxSoft Infra), Daniel (NyxSoft CTO)

00:00 Tom: okay hey everyone thanks for joining, we're here to do a deep dive on quantization tradeoffs for the models you mentioned — 13B finetuned customer support model and some routes for a 70B assistant. quick round robin?
00:12 Alicia: yeah hi i'm alicia, ML lead at nyxsoft. our main concerns are latency under 200ms 90p for small prompt paths and no more than 2% accuracy regression on our NLU intents.
00:24 Marcus: infra — we run a VPC with strict egress rules, and on-prem is an option if the security bar can't be met.
00:33 Tom: great, priya will lead technical. priya?
00:36 Priya: hey all, quick agenda — int8/fp8 perf and accuracy, gptq and awq comparison, effects on kv cache and batching, then piloting in your VPC. starting with int8 vs fp8: int8 is generally smaller and cheaper but needs calibration and can induce distribution shift on activation sensitive layers, fp8 gives better numeric dynamic range but is more hardware dependent — fewer runtimes support fp8 efficiently today.
01:05 Alicia: when you say fp8 hardware dependent, do you mean we need specific nvidia ampere-plus features or specialized cards?
01:13 Priya: yeah some vendors expose fp8 kernels on Hopper/Ampere with newer cuDNN; on-prem customers using older hardware won't see the latency gains. Redwood hosted has fp8 backend on select instance types, dedicated customers can request those too, but it's a committed capacity ask.
01:30 Daniel: our 70B assistant might be best served with fp8 if accuracy holds. 13B is more cost sensitive so int8 could be ok. but worried about the hallucination increase after aggressive quant.
01:40 Priya: that's expected — aggressive 4-bit gptq sometimes introduces edge-case regressions. AWQ (adaptive weight quant) tends to keep accuracy better on language modeling tasks for some architectures because it treats outlier weights differently. in our internal tests AWQ reduced perplexity delta by about 0.5-1.2 points vs straight GPTQ on certain 13B models, but results vary.
02:05 Marcus: how does that interact with kv cache behaviour? we depend on long convo contexts and we can't afford cold-start latency spikes.
02:12 Liam: good question — kv cache is mostly memory and kernel-level; quantization affects the math but not the cache format itself. where you see impacts is in transformer layer outputs precision; if quantized matmuls accumulate more rounding noise, you can see slower kv accumulation quality degradation over long sequences. that can show as drift in generation quality for long contexts.
02:40 Alicia: any mitigation?
02:42 Priya: prefix caching + hybrid schemes — keep the first N tokens or certain layers in higher precision (fp16) and quantize the rest. Redwood runtime supports per-layer mixed precision and selective dequantization for the KV cache. also continuous batching matters — batching can mask latency variance but increases median latency if not tuned.
03:10 Tom: latency SLOs — nyxsoft wants 200ms 90p on short prompts. with int8 on Dedicated our numbers for 13B on T4-class equiv showed median 80ms and p90 160ms at 8 concurrent qps with batching 4. fp8 on optimized hardware reduced median to 60ms and p90 120ms but with 15-20% higher instance cost.
03:40 Daniel: that sounds promising. what's the expected accuracy delta for intent classification if we go GPTQ 4-bit vs AWQ 4-bit?
03:48 Priya: for the finetuned 13B we saw 0.8-2.5% intent accuracy drop with vanilla GPTQ 4-bit. AWQ tends to be at the lower end, like 0.5-1.0% for the same setups in our evals. these are rough numbers, we need your prompt set to verify.
04:10 Alicia: ok we'll provide top intents and thresholds.
04:15 Marcus: network — pilot in VPC: do you require any special ports? and can the runtime be air-gapped?
04:22 Tom: Redwood Private supports on-prem and VPC peering. for the pilot we can run a Dedicated pool inside your VPC via our private control plane; we need egress for control plane management to specific IPs and port 443, SAML SSO connectivity, and outbound to our metrics collector if you opt in. fully air-gapped is possible with our on-prem bundle but takes more lead time.
04:55 Liam: small note — quantized checkpoints are larger to package sometimes due to sharding, but storage overhead is manageable. also model variant fallbacks: runtime can route to fp16 model if quality falls below a threshold.
05:10 Alicia: what's the regression detection? can we do A/B testing?
05:14 Priya: yes — Redwood Optimize has eval hooks. you can register prompt sets and acceptance criteria; we run continuous evals and fire regression alerts. for pilot we recommend canary route 10% traffic to quantized model and compare intent metrics.
05:35 Marcus: about batching — we run spikes to 120 qps during peak; how will batching affect p95 under burst?
05:43 Priya: batching adds a tiny queueing delay to reach fill, with dynamic batching we keep small batch windows so under burst the p95 may rise but p90 stays OK. For spikes you can set burst capacity and fallback to more instances. Dedicated has burst options.
06:05 Daniel: do we have any public numbers for AWQ vs GPTQ for the 70B family?
06:12 Priya: AWQ is newer; for many 70B-family models AWQ 4-bit keeps perplexity closer to fp16 than GPTQ does, but it depends on tokenizer and model architecture. we have internal spreadsheets — i'll share the benchmark sheet (link) with sample rows and error bars.
06:35 Alicia: (interrupting) sometimes transcriptions miss names — haha — but yeah please share.
06:40 Tom: quick caveat on HF/GPTQ toolchain versions — using different qconfig or group size can change outcomes; we recommend reproducible notebooks.
06:50 Priya: also watch out for quantizing LoRA adapters — if your finetune uses adapters they should be quantized carefully or kept in fp16, otherwise you can see outsized degradations.
07:05 Marcus: our infra team wants the security checklist — KMS, audit logs, SSO.
07:10 Tom: we'll attach SOC2, ISO docs and the network diagram. Redwood Private supports KMS/HSM integrations and audit logs with retention options.
07:25 Alicia: ok final practical ask — can you run the following: GPTQ 4-bit + AWQ 4-bit on our 13B finetuned model, measure intent accuracy on our top 100 prompts, and provide per-prompt diffs?
07:38 Priya: yes. we'll run that as first experiment. we'll also try a hybrid mixed-precision cache for the long convo paths.
07:45 Daniel: timeline?
07:47 Tom: we'll aim to have initial results in about a week to 10 days — so meeting again mid-next week for review.
07:55 Alicia: perfect. thanks everyone.
07:58 Tom: recap: Priya runs quant tests; Marcus provides data and network access details; Tom sends pricing and docs; Alicia annotates prompt thresholds. next call scheduled after bench results.
08:12 (meeting ends)
